name: Eat App Review Management
oneLiner: Review management add-on inside Eat App, a Dubai-based restaurant reservation, table management and guest CRM platform; it gathers reviews into one view, lets staff reply in the app and asks guests for reviews after their visit.
bestFor: Restaurants already using (or choosing) Eat App for reservations and guest CRM that want basic review monitoring and replies in the same system, rather than a standalone reputation platform.

updates.text: Acquired ReserveGo, an Indian table reservation platform serving more than 1,000 restaurants (acquisition dated June 2025 by PitchBook; announced publicly in January 2026).
Raised a $10M Series B extension led by PSG Equity through its portfolio company Zenchef, and announced a Swiggy partnership in India selling Eat App's growth suite as GroMax.

features: Reviews from Google, Bing and Facebook collected in one dashboard
Reply to reviews from inside Eat App
Post-visit guest feedback requests that route happy guests to leave a public review
Review analytics to understand guest sentiment by venue
Built on Eat App's reservations, table management and guest CRM, so feedback sits next to guest profiles
Online bookings from partner channels (e.g. Mozrest, Tripadvisor) flow into the same system

pricing.text: Eat App lists a free plan and paid tiers on its pricing page, with review management sold as an add-on; exact figures vary by region and could not be confirmed on the vendor page (third-party listings show review management at about $15/month).

notes: Review management is an add-on to the reservation platform, not a standalone product, as the current review already says. PSG/Zenchef led the January 2026 round; this is an investment, not an acquisition, as far as sources show (CB Insights dates the investment July 2025). Dropped from the current review: 'Free plan for 30 guests/month', 'reputation management from $15/month', 'smart reporting from $39/month' and 'email marketing from $39/month' (vendor page not confirmed; third-party sources conflict on plan prices and free-plan limits). Caution for the writer: Eat App describes sending only high-rating guests to Google (review gating), which Google's policies discourage. Customer names come from 2021 Eat App press materials. WebFetch blocked; facts from search results.
